lede.text: What each deal costs, how long the club controls him and what he's worth

because.label: How to read it
because.value: Figures are the most likely value with the range they could be; the range is in each figure's help tag.

because.label: Player
because.value: Every name opens his own window, with the full value breakdown.

because.label: 2040 salary
because.value: What he's paid this season, as the export states it.

because.label: Signed through
because.value: The last season his contract covers, a signed extension included. Options and clauses are listed with his row.

because.label: Service
because.value: Major-league service in years.days: 2.126 is two years and 126 days of a service year, not 2.1 years. 2.xxx means only whole years are exported.

because.label: Free agent after
because.value: The last season the club controls him, through his contract, arbitration or renewal. Two seasons means the later one may itself be free agency (an option, or service that crosses the line only if he stays up).

because.label: 2041 cost
because.value: What next season costs the club: his salary if a contract covers it, or the projected arbitration or renewal salary, most likely with the range it could be. A projection isn't committed money. "If kept" means he may leave instead.

because.label: 2041 wins
because.value: His projected wins above replacement (WAR) next season, most likely with the range it could be.

because.label: Contract value
because.value: What this contract is worth to any team that holds it: the wins he's projected to add, priced at what a win costs on this league's free-agent market, minus the salary still to be paid. Seasons further out count a little less (5% a year). Positive means he's worth more than he's paid; negative means he's paid more than his wins are worth. This is the view that matters in a trade.

because.label: Keeping him
because.value: Keeping him compared with replacing him with a minimum-salary player. Money you owe either way (a guaranteed contract is paid even if he's released) doesn't count, because it's spent no matter what; so a big contract never makes keeping him look better or worse. Only costs you'd avoid by moving on count, like future arbitration raises or an option you'd pick up. Positive means he's still the better use of the roster spot. Salary already paid this season counts in neither view.

because.label: Our view
because.value: His contract value read through the club's philosophy: how it weighs near seasons against far ones, risk, salary, club control and guaranteed money. "Same" means the philosophy doesn't lean on him.

because.label: How current
because.value: Pennant's copy of the league is from May 6, 2040. It couldn't find your OOTP save to compare dates with, so it can't tell whether the export is current: service time, control and the figures built on them are read as the export states them.

because.label: What it leaves out
because.value: The export's freshness could not be checked against the save.
